agenda_items.title: Call to order and moment of reflection
agenda_items.minutes:
The Council of the City of Ottawa met at Andrew S. Haydon Hall, 110 Laurier Avenue West, Ottawa, on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, beginning at 10:00 a.m. The Mayor, Mark Sutcliffe, presided over the meeting from Council Chambers with some Members attending in person and the remaining Members participating remotely by Zoom.
Mayor Sutcliffe led Council in a moment of reflection.

agenda_items.title: Motions of Which Notice Has Been Previously Given

sub_agendas_items.title: Trump Avenue Street Name Change

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the Central Park neighbourhood in Ottawa’s River Ward, was built in the late 1990s and early 2000s; and
WHEREAS many of the streets in Central Park were named after New York City landmarks, locations and an individual; and
WHEREAS one of the streets in the neighbourhood is named Trump Avenue, after Donald J. Trump, a New York City real estate mogul at the time of the naming and current President of the United States of America; and
WHEREAS the Central Park street naming theme was not proposed as a commemorative naming initiative and simply thematically named; and
WHEREAS Trump Avenue today would not meet any of the criteria had it gone through a formal commemorative naming process; and
WHEREAS City of Ottawa prides itself on who it commemorates and honours; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa's street naming policies require all new and replacement street names to be evaluated against established street naming criteria, including public safety and wayfinding considerations, to ensure that proposed names do not duplicate, sound the same as, or create confusion with existing or reserved street names and to support effective emergency response, navigation, and municipal addressing functions.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council approve the renaming of Trump Avenue; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that City Council direct the Councillor for Ward 16, River Ward, to lead a public consultation process with all households of Trump Avenue that will ultimately nominate a new street name that meets the City’s street naming policies, which may retain a New York City theme or propose a name that deviates from that theme; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the proposed new street name be recommended to City Council for approval no later than Q2 of 2027.

sub_agendas_items.title: Municipal Support for a National Plan to Reduce and End Homelessness
Ottawa Community Housing Corporation Temporary Financing for Capital Repairs

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS Ottawa Community Housing Corporation (OCHC) is the City of Ottawa's wholly-owned municipal housing corporation, which manages approximately two-thirds of the social housing stock under the administration of the City, and provides housing to approximately 32,000 residents; and WHEREAS on October 8, 2025 through report ACS2025-CSS-GEN-012, Council approved the refinancing of five Public Housing properties between 2026 and 2028, expected to generate approximately $133 million for urgent and critical capital repairs within the OCHC portfolio; and
WHEREAS the timing of capital repair expenditures may not align with the receipt of mortgage refinancing proceeds, or other long-term financing sources, creating a need for interim financing to advance necessary repair work; and
WHEREAS the City has access to short-term financing instruments at rates that could be lower than the borrowing rates OCHC would have access to; and
WHEREAS short-term financing to OCHC is permitted and consistent with section 107 of the Municipal Act, 2001, provided that Council determines the financing to be in the interests of the City; and
WHEREAS the provision of temporary financing to OCHC for capital repairs supports the Term of Council Priority for the preservation and maintenance of affordable and social housing assets owned by OCHC, and assists the City in fulfilling its obligations as Service Manager under the Housing Services Act, 2011 and is therefore considered to be in the interest of the City;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve the provision of temporary short-term financing by the City of Ottawa to Ottawa Community Housing Corporation, through the issuance of Promissory Notes or other short-term borrowing instruments, to finance capital repairs within the OCHC housing portfolio pending the receipt of mortgage refinancing proceeds, CMHC funding, or other long-term financing sources; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that all principal and interest associated with such temporary financing shall be repaid to the City by OCHC from operating revenues, or other available OCHC funding sources, such that the temporary financing does not result in an additional financial burden to City taxpayers; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Chief Financial Officer/Treasurer be delegated the authority to negotiate, execute, and administer all necessary agreements, Promissory Notes, repayment agreements, and related documents required to implement such temporary financing.

sub_agendas_items.title: City of Ottawa contribution to Canadian Red Cross appeal for July 2026 flood-impacted residents
sub_agendas_items.description: Note: The Sutcliffe/Johnson Motion of which Notice was previously given at the September 9, 2026, City Council meeting was replaced with the following revised motion pursuant to Subsection 59(5) of the Procedure By-law.

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS more than 6,500 Ottawa households continue to cope with the significant emotional, physical, and financial impacts of flooding to their homes arising from the July 1, 2026 extreme weather and flood event; and
WHEREAS the Canadian Red Cross has been assisting hundreds of residents and families in need since July 1, helping them meet basic needs, access supports, navigate complex insurance claims and restore their homes; and
WHEREAS the Canadian Red Cross has now gained a greater understanding of the extent of the financial hardship that hundreds of uninsured and underinsured residents are facing and will continue to face in the coming months and years; and
WHEREAS the Government of Canada announced on September 4, 2026 that it was establishing a donation matching program in response to the Canadian Red Cross donation appeal campaign for flood-impacted residents in Ottawa, in order to maximize donations and help our residents in need get back on their feet;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council institute a similar mechanism to match all donations from Canadian individuals and corporations made through the Canadian Red Cross appeal campaign, applied retroactively to the launch day of the appeal campaign on July 15, and up until the Canadian Red Cross closes the appeal; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED the City’s total contribution to the donation campaign up to $250,000, to be funded from the Tax Stabilization Reserve; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Canadian Red Cross report back to the City no later than Q2 2027 on how the funding helped flood-impacted residents in need.

agenda_items.title: Motions Requiring Suspension of the Rules of Procedure

sub_agendas_items.title: Advocating for the Expansion of the Disaster Recovery Assistance for Ontarians (DRAO) Program for Residents Impacted by Extreme Weather

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion in order to provide timely assistance to residents affected by recent extreme weather events.
WHEREAS the July 1, 2026 extreme rainfall event caused significant and wide-ranging flooding impacts across the City of Ottawa; and
WHEREAS City data indicates that rainfall totals varied significantly across Ottawa during the event, with some areas receiving more than 150 mm of rainfall, including areas that experienced a storm event close to or exceeding a 1 in 200-year event, and with the highest rainfall totals and intensities concentrated in central and southwest Ottawa; and
WHEREAS more than 7,500 Ottawa households continue to cope with the significant emotional, physical, and financial impacts of flooding to their homes arising from the July 1, 2026 extreme weather and flood event; and
WHEREAS on July 17, 2026, the Province activated the Disaster Recovery Assistance for Ontarians (DRAO) Program for a small portion of Ottawa residents impacted by the flooding in the Graham Creek/Stillwater Creek areas; and
WHEREAS the eligibility map for DRAO left out several neighbourhoods heavily impacted by the rains on July 1st, including Crystal Beach in Ottawa’s west end; and
WHEREAS since the DRAO program was activated for a small area in Ottawa in July, the City has continued to engage with provincial officials to provide information to support the expansion of the eligibility map to include more impacted areas; and
WHEREAS extreme weather events, including heavy rainstorms are becoming increasingly frequent and severe, and
WHEREAS municipalities across Ontario are seeing the impact of extreme weather and overland flooding, including the City of Toronto being hit with a “100 year storm”, consisting of 150 mm of torrential rain and severe flooding in some areas on September 2, 2026, and
WHEREAS action is needed at the provincial and federal level to support municipalities in responding to these increasingly frequent severe weather events, and
WHEREAS the current parameters for eligibility for the DRAO program do not reflect the lived reality of residents impacted by overland flooding from torrential rainstorms;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council direct staff to work with other municipalities in Ontario to request that the Province review the requirements for DRAO eligibility, to better reflect the experience and needs of impacted residents;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City Clerk send a copy of this resolution to the Premier of Ontario, the provincial Minister responsible for Emergency Preparedness and Response, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM).

sub_agendas_items.title: Municipal Disaster Recovery Assistance (MDRA) Program Application

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion so the City of Ottawa can apply for financial assistance through the Provincial Municipal Disaster Recovery Assistance (MDRA) program by the October 29, deadline.
WHEREAS on July 1, 2026, the City of Ottawa experienced intense rainfall over a short period of time, along with strong winds that caused widespread flooding and fallen trees; and
WHEREAS as a result of the July 1, 2026, weather event including extreme floods, the City experienced incremental capital and operating costs to repair public infrastructure and property and to protect public health, safety, and access to essential services; and
WHEREAS the provincial Municipal Disaster Recovery Assistance (MDRA) program helps municipalities recover from extraordinary costs after a natural disaster, and if the City applies, the program will be activated if eligible municipal costs are at least equal three percent of the municipalities own purpose taxation levy; and
WHEREAS the City is required to submit a resolution of Council and initial claim to the MDRA within 120 calendar days from the date of the onset of the disaster, which makes the deadline to apply October 29, 2026;
WHEREAS the City is currently compiling costs associated with the July 1, 2026, flooding event, and once completed and assessed, if the 3% threshold is met, must proceed with submitting its application for the MDRA program to the local Municipal Services Office as soon as possible in order to meet the provincial application deadline;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that if the City’s eligible costs meet the 3% threshold, Council endorse that the City of Ottawa apply to the Municipal Disaster Recovery Assistance (MDRA) program to recover eligible capital and operating costs incurred as a result of the July 1, 2026 flooding event; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the City Manager and General Manager and Chief Financial Officer, Finance and Corporate Services, be delegated the authority to verify and attest to the accuracy of the City’s MDRA claim and to finalize and submit all required application materials to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing as soon as possible.

sub_agendas_items.title: Special Event Road Closures and Community Notification
Private Approaches and Encroachments on Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive in Bel Air Heights

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS beginning in 2027/2028 the City will undertake an integrated road reconstruction project in the Bel-Air Community neighborhood of Ward 8, including the reconstruction of Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive; and
WHEREAS the project limits for the Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive Integrated Road, Sewer and Watermain project includes reinstating some private approaches and private encroachments on Whitmore Avenue (Iris Street to the north intersection with Cline Crescent), Cline Crescent (south intersection of Whitmore Avenue to Albany Drive) and Sherman Drive (Navaho Drive to Cline Crescent); and
WHEREAS some of the driveway widths/lengths within the project limits are not in full conformance with the City’s front yard parking restrictions and Private Approach By-law; and
WHEREAS, for existing properties, front yard parking restrictions and private approach by-law and private encroachments upon City Right-of-Way are normally enforced only on a complaint-driven basis; and
WHEREAS there have been no complaints with respect to non-compliant driveways (private approaches) or front-yard parking in this area; and
WHEREAS the area residents support providing relief for residents with existing driveways (private approaches) while acknowledging that any future driveways (private approaches) and front-yard parking must be in accordance with City by-laws;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council approve that, in respect of the reconstruction of Whitmore Avenue, Cline Crescent and Sherman Drive, private approaches and encroachments be reinstated as they were immediately prior to the reconstruction of this street, as practicable.

sub_agendas_items.title: Demolition Control Waiver for 72, 74, and 85 Pamilla Street

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa and the Developer (1197692 Ontario Inc.) have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding establishing the framework for a proposed land exchange whereby 72 and 74 Pamilla Street (total 750.89m²) would be conveyed to the City in exchange for 80 Norman Street (372.28 m²) allowing the City to create a larger neighbourhood park to replace the existing McCann Park; and
WHEREAS the owner of 425 Preston Street would provide 72 Pamilla Street (375.89 m²) and 74 Pamilla Street (375.00 m²) to the City and that the additional 378.61 m² land would contribute toward their parkland dedication if/when their assembled development lands are developed; and
WHEREAS the land being provided as parkland must be conveyed to the City free of all encumbrances; and
WHEREAS the demolition of existing residential use buildings at 72 and 74 Pamilla Street is required prior to transferring the properties to the City; and
WHEREAS the current state of 85 Pamilla, part of the future development site separate from the MOU, is in poor condition and not habitable; and
WHEREAS by waiving demolition control application, the City will not receive $6,200.48 (includes $1,274.64 Legal Fee + HST) which is the fee associated with a demolition control application; and
WHEREAS the properties remain subject to a demolition permit.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Council waive demolition control approval for the demolition of 72, 74 and 85 Pamilla Street and allow the applicant to proceed directly to demolition permits; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that 72 and 74 Pamilla Street be sodded, mulch-covered or soft landscaped following demolition and prior to transfer to the City, and 85 Pamilla Street be sodded and fenced, respectfully, in accordance with the Property Standards By-law; and
BE IT FURTHER REVOLVED that the waiver from Demolition Control be void if the corresponding demolition permits are not issued within two years of Council decision.
